name: roof-above-wired
notes: The roof-above machine with its clock BUILT (no command touches the machine after the build). Roof slab y 3..5 bedrock, target T [0,5,0]. Machine: A [0,6,0] piston facing west; X [1,7,0] stone; O [1,8,0] observer facing up; U [0,6,3] sticky piston facing north (extended at build), head [0,6,2], K [0,6,1] stone; crawl ceiling slab [0,7,-1]. Timing: Ro [1,9,0] repeater delay 1 facing west on top of O (O watches it); Ru [0,6,4] repeater delay 2 facing north into U's back. Both fed by the clock line S. Clock: a loop of two repeaters at delay 3 (R1 [8,6,0] facing west, R2 [8,6,2] facing east, dust [7,6,0..2] and [9,6,0..2]) carrying one 6-tick pulse: S = R1's output side, 6 ticks on / 6 off. Started by placing any block in front of the observer [10,6,1] (facing east): its 2-tick pulse goes into the loop and R1 stretches it to 6 ticks. S runs west from [6,6,0] to [5,6,0], climbs a staircase to Ro ([4,7,0] on [4,6,0], [3,8,0] on [3,7,0], [2,9,0] on [2,8,0]) and runs south then west along the roof to Ru ([5,6,1..5], [4..0,6,5]). On S's falling edge: Ro falls 2 ticks later, O fires 2 ticks after that and in the same tick Ru falls, so U pulls K away while O is on: A extends; O switches off silently before A's head lands; the landing arms A.
